summary:
I have at last been able to read “Science Fiction: A Hopeless Case—with Exceptions,” in SF Commentdr}. The article is every bit as fine as I had hoped it would be, and I wish to thank you for what you say about my work. I think I can shed a little light on why my work contains some of the “trash,” as you put it. America fiction is regional: the literary “Upper Realm” comes from the New York area; many of the long best sellers from the South, and from the West Coast where I live we had at one time, in San Francisco, what were called the beatnik writers. I am part of that last group, perhaps the only s-f writer who knew these men, such as Herbert Gold and the many San Francisco poets such as Robert Duncan and Jack Spicer and Gary Snyder—what I really wanted to do was their sort of thing, but I had read s-f as a kid and when I wrote I tended to write that more and more. One of my avant garde literary novels, from the ’50s, will be coming out, by the way, so you can judge what I might have been like as a beatnik literary type: it is called CONFESSIONS OF A CRAP ARTIST. I will 
try to get a copy to you (it will be a year from now). By you see, Mr. Lem, there is no culture here in California, only trash. And we who grew up here and live here and write here have nothing else to include as elements in our work; you can see this in ON THE ROAD. I mean it. The West Coast has no tradition, no dignity, no ethics— this is where that monster Richard Nixon grew up. How can one create novels...
